title: Isandro and the Harvest
premise: Astrid Fairweather, a hospice nurse who has spent twelve years rationalizing the backwards-counting whispers of the dying, inherits their estranged family's crumbling farmhouse in the village of Hollowmere. There they learn the Fairweathers have kept a covenant with something in the old well: each generation feeds it names, and in return the village prospers. When the melted church bell begins to ring and the dying of Hollowmere start counting toward zero, Astrid must decide whether to honor the family loyalty that protected them or expose the truth—ending with Astrid breaking the covenant, emptying the well at the cost of their own name being counted, and leading the villagers out before dawn.
about_author: Q. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former palliative care worker turned novelist who writes horror rooted in rural folklore and the ethics of care. They live near the coast with a deaf dog who, they insist, has never once heard the bell.

chapters.title: The Backwards Count
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the hospice, a dying man counts down from forty and stops at nine, and Astrid, as always, writes it off as neurological noise. A solicitor's letter arrives: Edith Fairweather is dead, and Astrid is named heir to Hollowmere. The emotional beat is the ache of being summoned by a family that erased them.

chapters.title: The House That Waits
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid arrives at the farmhouse, finding Edith's room preserved mid-countdown: a chalk wall of names, each struck through, the last one fresh. Neighbors watch from doorways but won't speak. The beat is dread dressed as grief; Astrid sleeps badly, hearing water where there is none.

chapters.title: What the Bell Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The village church has no bell—it was melted in 1911—yet at midnight it tolls, and every dog in Hollowmere goes silent. The vicar, Reverend Crane, warns Astrid gently to leave before the well refills. The beat is the first irrefutable crack in Astrid's rationalism.

chapters.title: Edith's Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with Edith's voice in letters. Astrid finds the covenant ledger: Fairweather names given to the well each generation, and payment recorded in harvests that never fail. Astrid learns their own childhood name is written in the ledger, uncrossed, reserved. The beat is betrayal—inheritance as a trap.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Alternating Astrid and villager Tam Osei's POV. Tam, whose grandmother was fed to the well in 1953, confirms the ledger and reveals the village's complicity: prosperity bought with neighbors. Astrid and Tam form a fragile alliance. The beat is the shame of loyalty—loving people who fed your family to a hole in the ground.

chapters.title: Nine Names
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The hospice deaths begin in Hollowmere itself: nine villagers start counting backwards in their sleep, all at the same pace. Crane admits the bell rings when the count nears zero—the well is choosing its tithe early because Edith died without delivering a name. The beat is mounting panic and Astrid's guilt.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The well, dry for decades, begins to rise, and the water shows faces. Tam's niece is among the nine counting. The villagers, desperate, turn on Astrid as the Fairweather who broke the covenant by existing. The beat is the corruption of power: fear making ordinary people into a mob.

chapters.title: Astrid Fairweather, Given
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid descends to the well to offer their own name and end it, hearing Edith's voice in the water: the covenant was never a bargain, only a leash the well holds on the whole village. The beat is the false climax—sacrifice offered, and refused, because the well wants a harvest, not a gift.

chapters.title: Breaking the Count
chapters.summary: Astrid and Tam's POV, interleaved. Astrid realizes the count runs backwards because the well is unwinding time to reclaim what it was owed; they poison the waterline with salt and the melted bell's clapper—recovered from the church foundations—shattering the covenant's anchor. The nine stop counting at one. The beat is desperate, costly triumph.

chapters.title: After the Harvest
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The village wakes barren for the first time in a century—no harvest, no whispers, no bell—and must learn to live unprospered and free. Astrid strikes their own name from the ledger, keeps Edith's letters, and stays as Hollowmere's nurse. The final beat: quiet, earned belonging, and one last dying patient who counts forward instead.
